week_1.text:
We audited 15 Google Ads accounts last month. 11 of them had broken conversion tracking.

Not small accounts. Companies spending $20K+/month with no idea which clicks actually convert.

Missing GTM tags. Unpublished containers. CAPI not connected. Conversion windows set to 1 day instead of 30.

The pattern was always the same:

→ Campaign setup was rushed because the media buyer was managing 4 other clients
→ Tracking was "I'll come back to it" and nobody came back
→ The campaign ran for weeks on broken data
→ When results looked bad, the team blamed the strategy

But the strategy was never the problem. The execution was compromised before the first impression served.

This is what we call the execution gap — the space between good strategy and flawed implementation.

When Synter's AI Agents set up a campaign, conversion tracking isn't a separate step. It's automatic:

→ Google Ads conversion action created
→ GTM tag configured with conversion label
→ GTM container published
→ Meta Pixel + CAPI connected
→ LinkedIn Insight tag installed

No checklist to forget. No "I'll do it later." Tracking is live before the campaign enables.

The media buyer's job is to define what success looks like. The agent makes sure it's measured correctly.

week_1.text:
The pricing model for ad tools is misaligned with results. Here's why we charge $49/month flat.

Most ad management platforms charge a percentage of ad spend — typically 3-10%. The more you spend, the more they charge.

The problem: this creates a perverse incentive. A tool that identifies $10K/month in wasted spend is financially motivated to not tell you about it.

We thought about this a lot before launching Synter.

Percentage-of-spend pricing means:
→ The tool benefits when you increase budget, regardless of performance
→ There's no incentive to find waste or recommend budget cuts
→ Small teams get priced out before they can prove ROI
→ Enterprise accounts subsidize product development while SMBs get a demo wall

Flat pricing at $49/month means:
→ We win when you win — our revenue comes from you staying, not spending more
→ We're incentivized to help you find waste and reallocate to what converts
→ Same tooling whether you manage $5K or $500K
→ You know the cost before you sign up

This isn't altruism. It's alignment.

When your tool makes more money from your efficiency gains (because you stay longer), it's structurally motivated to make you more efficient.

When your tool makes more money from your spend increases, ask yourself who it's really optimizing for.

6 months in, this is the decision we feel best about. The trust it builds is worth more than the percentage revenue we left on the table.

week_1.text:
We ran the same campaign across 5 platforms simultaneously. Here's what the data actually showed.

We wanted to answer a question every media buyer argues about: which platform delivers the best B2B leads?

So we set up an actual test. Same offer. Same audience definition. Same budget ($50/day per platform). Same creative concept adapted to each platform's specs.

Platforms: Google Search, Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, TikTok.

14-day results:

→ Reddit: $4.20 CPL — lowest cost, surprisingly high intent. Subreddit targeting (r/PPC, r/marketing) delivered people actively looking for solutions
→ TikTok: $6.10 CPL — the surprise performer. B2B marketers are on TikTok; they just don't act like it. Video ads outperformed static 3:1
→ Meta: $8.30 CPL — best creative testing environment. Lookalike audiences still work when seeded with quality data
→ Google: $11.50 CPL — most reliable and predictable. Brand search converts at 4x non-brand
→ LinkedIn: $38.00 CPL — highest cost, but lead quality was 2.5x better by pipeline conversion rate

The insight isn't that one platform "wins." It's that platform mix matters more than platform choice.

LinkedIn creates awareness among decision-makers. Google captures the intent LinkedIn generated. Reddit and TikTok fill the top of funnel at a fraction of the cost.

But here's the real finding: most teams only run 2 platforms because adding a third means another dashboard, another reporting format, another set of API quirks to learn.

The barrier to multi-platform isn't strategy. It's capacity.

That's the problem Synter solves. One interface across all platforms. Same campaign creation flow. Unified reporting. The strategic decision — which platforms to test — stays with the media buyer. The execution across all of them is handled by AI Agents.

week_2.text:
Synter's Campaign IDE is live — and it's not what you'd expect from an AI ad tool.

Most AI advertising tools go one of two ways:
→ Full autopilot: "Trust the AI, don't touch anything"
→ Suggestion engine: "Here's a recommendation, now go do it yourself"

Both miss what experienced media buyers actually want.

After talking to dozens of agency media buyers, we learned something: they don't want a black box OR a clipboard. They want speed with control.

So we built the Campaign IDE — borrowing the metaphor from software engineering.

How it works:
→ Start with natural language: "Create a search campaign for SaaS lead gen targeting marketing automation keywords, $50/day"
→ The agent builds the full campaign structure: keywords, ad groups, responsive search ads, bid strategy, geo targeting, conversion tracking
→ Everything appears in a visual editor where you can review, modify, approve each element
→ One click to launch across the platform

Conversational creation. Visual editing. Human approval. Instant execution.

The IDE doesn't replace the media buyer's judgment. It eliminates the 47 clicks between their decision and execution.

A senior strategist can now review and launch a fully configured campaign in 2 minutes instead of building one from scratch in 45.

That's what AI Agent Media Buyers actually means. Your expertise drives the strategy. The agent handles the implementation.

week_2.text:
AI agent tool selection is about to reshape how ad tech gets distributed.

Right now, if you build an advertising tool, your distribution depends on:
• A marketing site optimized for SEO
• G2 reviews and comparison pages
• Content marketing and thought leadership
• Paid ads (ironically)
• Word of mouth

All of that assumes a human is Googling "best ad management tool" and comparing options.

With MCP (Model Context Protocol), the AI agent picks the tool. The human never sees alternatives.

When a marketing director asks Claude to "set up our Q3 paid media campaigns," the agent routes to whichever MCP server can execute that action. There's no comparison page. No G2 review. No pricing page visit.

The user gets results. The tool gets usage. Everything in between disappears.

This is why we built Synter's MCP server to be the most capable execution layer in advertising:

→ 100+ executable actions across the full campaign lifecycle
→ 10+ ad platforms supported
→ Creative generation built in
→ Conversion tracking automated
→ OAuth credential injection and audit logging handled automatically

First-mover advantage in MCP isn't about having the best landing page. It's about being the most reliable, most complete execution layer that AI agents can depend on.

The agencies and tools that understand this shift will position themselves where the AI agents are looking — not where the humans are browsing.

week_2.text:
How we used Synter's own AI Agents to rebuild our entire paid media strategy in one afternoon.

Last month, our Google Ads performance had plateaued. Instead of spending a week on manual analysis, we connected Claude Code to Synter's MCP server and ran the full diagnostic.

In one session (about 30 minutes of conversation), the agent:

→ Pulled SimilarWeb competitive intelligence on 5 competitors
→ Discovered our paid search gap — competitors had <1% from paid, channel was wide open
→ Created 3 new search campaigns (AI Agent Category, Pain Points, CRM Integration)
→ Added 23 new keywords across existing campaigns
→ Launched competitor conquesting on 4 named competitors
→ Applied 30+ negative keywords across all campaigns
→ Set device bid adjustments based on GAQL conversion data (desktop converting at 2.4x)
→ Audited search terms and blocked $340/week in wasted clicks

Manual equivalent: 4-6 hours of work across SimilarWeb, Google Ads, and spreadsheets.

The results after 3 weeks:
→ CPA down 18% from device optimization alone
→ Competitor keywords converting at $8.40 CPA vs $34.20 on generics
→ $1,360/month in waste eliminated from negative keyword audit

We're not just building this tool. We're using it every day on our own campaigns.

That's the best feedback loop in product development — when your team's pain is your customer's pain.
